transcript: Okay, so how do I feel about Andrew Lloyd Webber's more popular musicals, like Phantom of the Opera, Evita, Jesus Christ Superstar, etcetera? I've talked a lot about how I am a certified Andrew Lloyd Webber hater, but I've never really explained what I don't like about him. So I'll start there, and then I'll loop back around to this question. And I will start by just saying that I actually think Andrew Lloyd Webber has written some really good songs. Like, when he is good, I think he is really, really good. In fact, I would say that Gesemini is one of my favorite musical theater songs of all time. However, my problem with a lot of Andrew Lloyd Webber shows is that in totality, a lot of them fall flat. For me. I think this is largely for two reasons. Number one largely comes down to personal preference. And it's that I just don't really like a lot of the things that he chooses to adapt into shows. Most of them are just not stories that I am particularly interested in. And that's totally okay. Number two is that I find that Andrew Lloyd Webber scores tend to be very repetitive, which is to say that he has a tendency to write four or five melodies and then just repeat those same melodies over and over and over again. And I find that even when I enjoy those melodies, watching that show from start to finish, I Tend to get bored of them after hearing them for the fourth or fifth time. I think that motifs in general can be really useful tool in musical theatre, but I find in Andrew's case a lot of his melodies don't really take on any new meaning as the show goes on, and it's mostly repetition for repetition's sake. The two shows of his that I think escaped this issue are Jesus Christ Superstar and Joseph, which in general have much more varied scores, and as a result, I actually think those are his two most successful scores, and probably the shows of his that I like the most. I would also be remiss if I didn't mention that I also don't think Angela Ludwig Webber is a particularly good person. I think that we saw this on full display with the Cinderella fiasco, and there are several other examples I won't go into here. I also think there are like one too many instances of his work allegedly being plagiarized from other sources. That feels more like a pattern of behavior than a coincidence. If I can give him credit for one thing, it's that in recent years he has been very unpretentious about his work. I do actually give him a lot of credit for allowing these bold new takes of his work, specifically Jamie Lloyd Sunset, uh, the rumored immersive fanum, leap of Faith, Cats. These revivals in particular I think have been some of the most Successful and exciting work that we have seen from him maybe in his entire career. To be honest, the only Webber shows that I've really loved have been those with a strong directorial vision that are able to elevate the show beyond just what is on the page. So to go back to the original question, when it comes to Phantom, I do really like a lot of the songs in isolation, but it definitely falls into that too repetitive category for me. Avita is one of the shows that I am actually not really familiar with at all, outside of a handful of songs like don't cry for me, Argentina, which hot take I think is kind of overrated. And like I said before, I think Jesus Christ Superstar is one of his most successful scores. But the show itself, I think, leaves a little bit to be desired. Tired. It doesn't really go any deeper than what if we told the story of Jesus, but with rock music? Because apart from that, it is just a straightforward retelling of the story of Jesus, which is a story we've heard a million and one times.
